projects.name: Olist MLOps
projects.problem: Predict whether an Olist e-commerce order will arrive late, and serve that prediction through a tested, monitored API instead of a notebook.
built: A FastAPI inference service around the fitted scikit-learn model, with schema and semantic input checks.
Feature engineering shared by the training notebooks and the service, with a parity check between them.
Prometheus metrics, two alert rules and an offline score-drift check.
DVC pointers for data and model files, an MLflow registry entry, and a GitHub Actions pipeline.
works: CI runs lint, formatting, 172 tests and a Docker build on every push.
A Kaggle notebook re-runs the pipeline from the raw Olist data and reproduces the saved test results.
The service never refits the model; it loads the saved preprocessor and classifier.
projects.architecture: Six notebooks prepare data and train; a FastAPI service loads the saved preprocessor and model; Docker Compose runs the API with Prometheus.
projects.stack: Python, scikit-learn, FastAPI, Docker, Prometheus, DVC, MLflow, GitHub Actions

evidence.text: GitHub Actions run 42863988828: 172 passed, lint and format clean; reproduced from a fresh clone on 2026-11-14.
Kaggle re-run from the raw CSVs on 2026-11-14: test PR-AUC 0.0670 and ROC-AUC 0.6115, matching the saved model.
Feature parity on 14,470 validation rows and 821 features, maximum difference 0, measured on the original workstation.
Purchase-time availability of every feature is not verified, and there is no DVC remote.

projects.status: Educational project, not deployed. The model is weak: test ROC-AUC 0.61 at a 4.28% late rate.
projects.role: My project in an MLOps training course. The model-evaluation write-up and the Kaggle reproduction were added in November 2026 with an AI coding agent.

trace.name: Olist orders
trace.note: Public Olist orders, items, payments and reviews, joined into one row per order.

trace.name: Chronological split
trace.note: Train, validation and test periods are split by purchase date, so the test period is later than anything used for fitting.

trace.name: Shared features
trace.note: Deterministic feature code used by both the notebooks and the service; explicit future and target fields are blocked.

trace.name: Model and threshold
trace.note: Logistic regression chosen on validation PR-AUC; the decision threshold is chosen on validation only.

trace.name: Feature parity
trace.note: A script compares the service's features with the saved training matrix before a release.

trace.name: Inference API
trace.note: FastAPI single and batch prediction endpoints with input checks and a model fingerprint in every response.

trace.name: Monitoring
trace.note: Prometheus metrics and alert rules; the drift check reports insufficient data below 200 scores instead of claiming no drift.

decisions: Reported the weak test result (ROC-AUC 0.61, accuracy below an always-on-time baseline at the chosen threshold) instead of accuracy alone.
Chose the threshold on validation only and used the later test period once.
Documented the point-in-time leakage risk of historical aggregates instead of claiming real-time readiness.
Kept data and model files out of Git, tracked by DVC pointers, and stated that a fresh clone cannot serve predictions.
tested: 172 tests in GitHub Actions (run 42863988828), reproduced from a fresh clone on 2026-11-14.
Kaggle re-run from raw data: test PR-AUC 0.06704 and ROC-AUC 0.6115, matching the saved bundle.
Validation ROC-AUC 0.746 and PR-AUC 0.125; test ROC-AUC 0.611 and PR-AUC 0.067 at a 4.28% late rate.
limits: Not verified for purchase-time inference: some aggregates may include later updates.
No DVC remote or published model, so a fresh clone runs the tests but cannot serve predictions.
No alert notification channel and no store joining predictions with outcomes.
The model's predictive value is weak; the project's value is the inference engineering.

projects.name: EduSmartAI
projects.problem: An academic platform needed to warn about struggling students early, but its old 0.979 score relied on data only known after a course ended.
built: On a branch of a graduation project by @bahaaed07706: early-risk models for day 14, 28 and 42, using only data visible by that day.
Student-grouped validation, a temporal holdout and confidence intervals.
Shared feature code for training and serving, rule-based explanations and intervention tracking.
Token revocation, audit logging, rate limiting, and a PostgreSQL path.
works: Models retrained from the branch reproduce its reported results.
ROC-AUC rises from 0.566 at day 14, close to chance, to 0.729 at day 42.
Backend security, intervention and serving behavior pass their tests.
projects.architecture: FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend, scikit-learn pipelines per cut-off, and a React frontend with Arabic and English.
projects.stack: Python, FastAPI, scikit-learn, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, React

evidence.text: Retrained on 2026-11-07: ROC-AUC 0.566, 0.677 and 0.729, matching the report.
Backend tests: 220 passed, 3 skipped, at commit 73583aa.
Frontend tests and the live PostgreSQL integration were not run.

projects.status: Branch not merged. PR #7 was closed with no review.
projects.role: EduSmartAI is a graduation project by @bahaaed07706, who built and owns it. He had already documented that the old 0.979 was inflated by leakage, and he wrote the retriever. My branch builds the replacement models and the backend hardening around them. Its commits credit an AI coding agent as co-author.

trace.name: Course activity
trace.note: Attendance, submissions and engagement records for each student and course.

trace.name: Temporal cut-off
trace.note: At day 14, 28 or 42, only events visible by that day are used, which avoids the leakage in the old evaluation.

trace.name: Group-aware validation
trace.note: StratifiedGroupKFold keeps each student on one side of every split, with a temporal holdout and bootstrap confidence intervals.

trace.name: Early-risk model
trace.note: A scikit-learn pipeline per cut-off, trained so that scaling and encoding happen inside each fold.

trace.name: Train-serve parity
trace.note: Training and serving share one feature module, and tests check that they produce the same features.

trace.name: Explanation
trace.note: Deterministic, rule-based explanations of which signals drove a prediction, with no model-generated text.

trace.name: Intervention
trace.note: Staff can record and track actions taken for a flagged student.

decisions: Reported that the day-14 model is close to chance, and called it insufficient for operational use, instead of tuning until it looked better.
Built replacement models after the project owner documented the leakage in the old 0.979.
Added server-side token revocation, audit logging and rate limiting to the backend.
Added a bilingual held-out RAG evaluation, Arabic right-to-left support and accessibility work.
tested: ROC-AUC by cut-off: day 14, 0.5657. Day 28, 0.6769. Day 42, 0.7288.
Accuracy by cut-off: day 14, 0.5536. Day 28, 0.6444. Day 42, 0.6844.
Backend suite: 220 passed, 3 skipped, at commit 73583aa.
limits: The legacy 0.979 could not be reproduced, because a source file is not in the repository.
The branch is not part of the project's main branch.
The retriever is by the project owner, and it is lexical, not semantic.
Live LLM answer quality was not evaluated. Frontend tests and the live PostgreSQL integration were not run.

about: I am an AI Engineer in Amman with a B.Sc. in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence from Philadelphia University. The part of AI work I care about most starts after the first demo: can it be measured, can it be stopped, and what happens when something fails?

That is why my projects look the way they do. They track evidence, separate tenants and wait for approval. Most of them build on existing software instead of starting from nothing, and each one says so. I also use AI coding agents in my work, and the project pages say where that is known.

approach.title: Measure before claiming
approach.text: Evaluation comes with the system, and a missing measurement stays missing.

approach.title: Keep authority out of the model
approach.text: Scope and permissions live in server code, where a prompt cannot change them.

approach.title: Give automation a stopping point
approach.text: Risky steps wait for a check or a person, and retries cannot repeat them.

approach.title: Report what the data supports
approach.text: When a strong number comes from a flawed test, I replace it and explain why.

co2.title: Vehicle CO2: the same model, scored more strictly
co2.lead: The notebook reported R² 0.9972. 1,103 of its 7,385 rows are exact duplicates, so some test rows had a copy in training. Select a step to see what changed.

steps.name: Notebook split, duplicates kept
steps.note: The original result, reproduced. 246 of the 1,477 test rows have an identical copy in the training set.

steps.name: Duplicates removed, same split
steps.note: Removing duplicates first raises the typical error by about half a gram per kilometre.

steps.name: Whole vehicle models held out
steps.note: Five-fold GroupKFold by make and model: the model never sees the vehicle it is scored on. This is the honest figure.

steps.name: Baseline: one straight line
steps.note: A straight line on fuel consumption and fuel type. The model beats it, by less than the first score suggested.

co2.takeaway: R² barely moves, from 0.9972 to 0.9948. The typical error grows by a third, from 3.03 to 4.04 g/km, and stays below the baseline's 5.82.

olist.title: Olist MLOps: the model against chance
olist.lead: Late deliveries are 4.28% of test orders. A model that guesses at random scores about that rate on PR-AUC, and 0.5 on ROC-AUC.
olist.takeaway: Better than chance, and weak. The project's value is the tested, monitored service around the model, and the page says so.
